chapter: Three D's and Bay Area struggles
title: Aside about Weatherwax's friend Georgia Frontiere
summary: A side conversation about a wealthy supporter of the Brubeck Institute, with Gioia saying it will be edited out.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He’s involved with a young lady named Georgia Frontiere, who owns the St. Louis Rams . . .
I know who Georgia Frontiere, sure
Primarily they live in Sedona and St. Louis. She just bought a private rail car. They’re going to be in Malibu in . . .
When we play at Pepperdine, we usually stay in their Malibu [home], if it’s offered to us. I don’t know if we should say she owns 36 homes.
We will edit that out of the transcript. Things like this we will edit out. They don’t need to go into the Smithsonian.
And that’s not counting the new railroad car.
And you better not mention Georgie. But she’s really interested in helping the Institute too. Don’t you think?
And he is too. They have become very close friends, and yet I always feel you have to protect her, and him, because . . .
She was an opera singer at one time.
Last time we were at dinner, she said to me, “Russell, life is so strange. I started off life singing in an opera chorus, and now I own an NFL team.”
